title: Set 188

sentences.ko: 그래, 네가 보자던 프로 보자. 근데 또 처음 한 시간 동안 아무 일도 안 일어나는 거면 나 그냥 잘 거야.
sentences.text: Fine, we can watch your thing, but if it's another one where nothing happens for the first hour, I'm going to bed.

alts.text: Okay, we'll watch your show, but if nothing happens for the first hour again, I'm going to bed.
Very well, we may watch your selection, but if it is another one in which nothing happens during the first hour, I will be going to bed.

sentences.note: **another one where** 는 또 그런 식인 것, 즉 같은 부류가 하나 더 나온다는 뜻이에요. **I'm going to bed** 는 자러 갈 거야라는 말로, 불평 섞인 경고에 자주 써요.

sentences.ko: 한 달쯤은 기타에 완전 빠져 있었는데, 손가락이 아프기 시작해서 일주일 쉬었거든. 그랬더니 지금은 그냥 구석에 세워져서 나 죄책감만 들게 해.
sentences.text: I was really into the guitar for like a month, but then my fingers started hurting, so I took a week off, and now it's just sitting in the corner making me feel guilty.

alts.text: I was super into guitar for like a month, then my fingers started hurting, so I took a week off, and now it just sits in the corner guilt-tripping me.
I was quite enthusiastic about the guitar for approximately a month; however, my fingers began to hurt, so I took a week off, and now it simply sits in the corner and makes me feel guilty.

sentences.note: **into** 는 무언가에 푹 빠져 있다는 뜻이에요. casual 의 **guilt-tripping** 은 죄책감을 느끼게 만든다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 응, 미안, 오늘 아침에 지하철이 엄청 느렸어. 아니 그 앞 차만 탔어도 괜찮았을 텐데, 뭐, 못 탔지.
sentences.text: Yeah, sorry, the train was super slow this morning. I mean, if I'd caught the one before it I would've been fine, but, you know, I didn't.

alts.text: Sorry, sorry, train was crazy slow this morning. If I'd made the earlier one I'd have been fine, but yeah, I didn't.
I apologize; the train was extremely slow this morning. Had I caught the previous one, I would have arrived on time, but unfortunately I did not.

sentences.note: **if I'd caught the one before it** 은 그 앞 차를 탔더라면이라는 지나간 일에 대한 가정이에요. **caught** 는 버스나 기차를 시간 맞춰 잡아탄다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 아래층 가게 이제 샌드위치 하나에 8달러 받는 거 봤어? 내가 여기 처음 들어왔을 때는 5달러쯤이었는데, 샌드위치가 커진 것도 아니잖아.
sentences.text: Did you see they want eight dollars for a sandwich at the place downstairs now? It was like five when I started working here, and it's not like the sandwiches got any bigger.

alts.text: The place downstairs wants eight bucks for a sandwich now, did you see? It was like five when I started here, and the sandwiches sure didn't get any bigger.
Have you noticed that the restaurant downstairs now charges eight dollars for a sandwich? It was approximately five dollars when I began working here, and the sandwiches have not become any larger.

sentences.note: **they want eight dollars** 는 8달러를 달라고 한다, 즉 그 값을 받는다는 말이에요. **it's not like** 는 ~한 것도 아니잖아라며 따질 때 써요.

sentences.ko: 잠깐, 너 아직 그 회사 다녀, 아니면 드디어 그만뒀어? 지난번에 봤을 때 계속 그만둘 거라고 해서 농담인지 진짜인지 모르겠더라.
sentences.text: Wait, are you still at that same job, or did you finally leave? Last time I saw you, you kept saying you were going to quit, and I couldn't tell if you were kidding.

alts.text: Hang on, you're still at that job? Or did you finally quit? Last time I saw you, you kept saying you were gonna quit, and I couldn't tell if you were joking.
Just a moment, are you still in the same position, or did you eventually leave? When I last saw you, you repeatedly said that you intended to resign, and I could not tell whether you were joking.

sentences.note: **I couldn't tell if** 는 ~인지 아닌지 알 수가 없었다는 뜻이에요. **kidding** 은 농담하다로, joking 과 같은 뜻이에요.

reviewed: 다섯째 문장 formal 의 Excuse me 는 상대 말을 따지거나 끼어들 때 쓰는 말이라 잠깐이라는 뜻이 아님. Just a moment 로 바꾸고, working at the same position 은 전치사가 어색해 in the same position 으로 고침
다섯째 문장 casual 의 Or'd you 는 글자로 적으면 알아보기 힘든 축약이라 Or did you 로 고침
